The paper titled "Temporal Network Analysis of Microservice Architectural Degradation" discusses how temporal networks arise in microservice systems when analyzing the architecture across different releases or monitoring a deployed system using tracing. It also explores the study of networks as evolving over time and the challenges in obtaining and analyzing temporal networks from microservice systems. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11571?utm_source=openai))

Additionally, the paper "System States Forecasting of Microservices with Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Data" addresses the dynamic and complex spatio-temporal relationships among microservice instances, highlighting the importance of considering both spatial and temporal dimensions in system state prediction. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07894?utm_source=openai))

These sources collectively cover the mentioned information in the context of microservice systems and temporal networks.  No source extracted due to invalid syntax

The paper titled "A Tight Lower Bound for Doubling Spanners" discusses the transformation of the net-tree spanner into a spanner with lightness \(\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-(d+1)})\) in doubling metrics. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11555?utm_source=openai))

It also establishes that in doubling metrics, any \((1+\epsilon)\)-spanner must have lightness \(\tilde{\Omega}(\epsilon^{-(d+1)})\). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11555?utm_source=openai))

Additionally, the paper presents a construction of a \((1+\epsilon)\)-spanner with \(\tilde{O}(n \cdot \epsilon^{-d})\) edges in doubling metrics. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11555?utm_source=openai))

These results are detailed in the paper "A Tight Lower Bound for Doubling Spanners" by An La, Hung Le, Shay Solomon, Cuong Than, Vinayak, Shuang Yang, and Tianyi Zhang, published on August 15, 2025. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11555?utm_source=openai))  No source extracted due to invalid syntax
